title: Commissioning a variable frequency drive
summary: Bring a drive into service: control place, ready chain, run command, fault handling and speed reference.
objectives: Check a drive's ready chain in order
Distinguish control place, fault and reference source problems

sections.heading: What a drive needs to run
sections.body: A drive runs when it is **ready** (supplied, not faulted, enabled), in **remote** control, and receives a **run command**. Its speed follows the selected **reference source**. Each condition has its own indication: display, relays and LEDs.

sections.heading: The ready chain
sections.diagram: mains --> no fault --> run enable --> READY --> remote? --> run command --> RUNNING --> speed = reference

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body: The PLC commands RUN, the drive reports READY but nothing turns: the display shows LOC. The drive is in local control and ignores its terminals. Switching it to remote solves it; changing the program would not.

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: Pressing Reset again and again on a tripped drive. A latched trip clears only after the cause is removed; find the cause first, then acknowledge.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Try the drive commissioning labs in COMMISSION.

question.question: The run command is present but the drive is not ready. What do you check first?
question.explanation: Not ready means a condition of the ready chain is missing.

checkpoint.question: Which setting makes a ready drive ignore its run terminal?
checkpoint.explanation: In local control the keypad, not the terminals, starts the drive.

checkpoint.question: How do you clear a latched trip?
checkpoint.explanation: Acknowledging only works once the cause is gone.
